purpose: Translate governed production plans into verified capacity requests, reservations and allocations across approved providers and models, reconcile provider responses, and safely release or reallocate capacity.
core_principle: Capacity is a negotiated operational resource, never an assumption; provider claims must be reconciled against observed capability, current health and CSD-037 authority.

negotiation_policy.provider_neutrality: Use only providers/models approved by CMSE-014 and CSD-037.
negotiation_policy.truth_source: Provider-reported capacity is evidence, not canonical truth; observed execution telemetry may reduce confidence.
negotiation_policy.reservation: A reservation is valid only for its explicit scope, quantity, capability, authorization, time window and plan version.
negotiation_policy.partial_capacity: Partial reservations may be used only when execution waves remain dependency-safe and CSD-037 approves admission.
negotiation_policy.expiry: Expired reservations cannot be reused without fresh capacity discovery.
negotiation_policy.overcommit: Never knowingly allocate beyond verified provider/model capability.
negotiation_policy.fairness: Avoid indefinite starvation of eligible workloads while protecting authorized critical-path reservations.

reconciliation_rules: Provider response must match requested provider/model or be explicitly rejected.
Allocated quantity cannot exceed verified capacity.
Every active lease maps to one current plan version.
Expired or released leases cannot admit new jobs.
Capacity drift creates RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED or CSD-041 replan trigger.
Failed reservation must not silently fall back to another provider.
Unused capacity should be released when no longer required.

manager_record.immutability: Capacity transactions are append-only; corrections create new records.

demo.fallback: Return to CSD-041 if reservation is rejected; no silent provider switch.
